newsitem.title: USA: Mead says Q1 results reflect lower prices.
newsitem.headline: Mead says Q1 results reflect lower prices.

text.p: Mead Corp on Wednesday attributed a decline in first quarter earnings to lower prices for many of its products.

"Our results reflect steep price declines for corrugating medium, lower prices for coated paper, and lower prices and sales volumes within our distribution business," said chairman and chief executive Steven Mason.
Mead Corp said Wednesday first quarter net dropped to $20.2 million, or $0.38 per share, from $36.3 million, or $0.68 cents per share, for the same period in 1996.
First quarter 1996 net earnings per share included a 10-cent gain from the sale of a discontinued business.
The company reported first quarter 1997 sales increased six percent to $1.14 billion because of the company's acquisition in November 1996 of a coated and specialty paper mill in Rumford, Maine.

"Despite difficult markets, Mead's businesses achieved strong sales volume and productivity for the quarter, especially in the Publishing Paper, Fine Paper, Specialty Paper, and School and Office Products divisions, and in our Coated Board System," Mason said.
Sales revenue in the company's paper segment was higher than in the first quarter of 1996.

Mead said even without the Rumford acquisition, sales revenue was ahead of last year on much higher volume, despite lower prices for coated groundwood and uncoated paper, but earnings were below prior-year levels.
Packaging and paperboard sales and earnings for the segment declined on significantly lower prices for corrugating medium.
The school and office products segment declined on lower prices and reduced sales volume in the Zellerbach division.
Results for Mead's jointly owned Northwood companies improved from the prior year period on higher pulp shipments, although pulp prices were down substantially from the year-earlier period.

The company repurchased approximately 125,000 common shares during the quarter and has now repurchased more than 2.1 million shares under the five million share repurchase authorization of April, 1995.
Mead said backlogs remain strong in coated paper and demand remains steady in the company's carbonless, specialty, coated board, and school and office products businesses.
